note: Curated candidates for Mallowstead-origin contract workloads. Prices are OpenRouter list-price snapshots and may vary by provider/discount. Benchmark-recorded actual cost is authoritative after a run.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731
models.why: Primary value candidate: very low token cost, 1M context, strong reasoning/agent performance, and recent GA revision.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
models.why: Strong quality reference at a still practical price; especially interesting for contract following and lightweight agentic work.

models.name: MiniMax M2.5
models.why: Good agent/instruction benchmark profile and notably low structured-output error rates on some OpenRouter providers.

models.name: Qwen3.5 Flash 02-23
models.why: Extremely cheap 1M-context candidate. Public structured-output error telemetry makes it especially interesting for our contract benchmark.

models.name: Mistral Small 4
models.why: Cheap and very fast; useful to test whether a smaller generalist already clears the formal contracts reliably.

models.name: Qwen3.5 35B A3B
models.why: Efficient MoE mid-tier Qwen; useful comparison against Qwen3.5 Flash without jumping to the expensive 397B model.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813
models.why: Higher-capability DeepSeek control point; tells us whether Pro buys meaningful contract reliability over V4 Flash.

models.name: Gemini 3 Flash Preview
models.why: More expensive quality/agentic reference with strong instruction-following and structured-output support.

models.name: GLM 5.2
models.why: Long-horizon agent/workflow specialist; worth checking on large utility and timelapse contracts despite the higher output price.

models.name: Kimi K2.5
models.why: Adds a distinct strong conversational/agentic family and is particularly worth testing on Character rather than only Utility.
